standard.title: Plan and negotiate with others
standard.description: participate in activities that involve planning and negotiating with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can participate in collaborative planning activities using familiar phrases and modelled structures (AC9LS4C02). They allocate tasks and follow sequences. They have not yet used language to express and negotiate preferences and ideas — only to coordinate task allocation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in planning and negotiation activities that require expressing preferences and ideas, checking understanding, delegating and managing decisions in the target language.

nodes.label: Expressing preferences and ideas in planning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express preferences and ideas in collaborative planning contexts — contributing personal views and negotiating with others about options and decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least two preferences or ideas in a planning activity and respond to at least one partner's preference or idea.
nodes.typical_width: Express and negotiate preferences across planning contexts; check understanding and progress during tasks; delegate roles and tasks; develop questions for guests or interviews; promote participation in events using target language.
wider: Lead a planning negotiation — ensure all group members contribute a preference and that the final decision reflects genuine compromise
Conduct a simulated transaction involving genuine negotiation over options and decisions
nodes.hinge_reason: Expressing preferences in collaborative contexts — contributing personal views not only allocating tasks — is what distinguishes planning from coordination. Students who cannot negotiate preferences cannot engage with the opinion-exchange demands that continue through subsequent bands.

response_modes.reason: Preference expression in planning requires students to move from describing tasks to advocating for options. Structured planning tasks with open decision points scaffold this move.

success_criteria: Expresses at least two preferences or ideas in a collaborative planning task
Responds to a partner's contribution — building on, questioning or negotiating rather than simply accepting

nodes.label: Problem-solving and decision-making in collaborative tasks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in planning tasks that involve decision-making with constraints — budgets, quantities, priorities — using target language to justify choices and reach agreement.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a decision-making task using the target language — expressing at least two justified choices and contributing to a shared outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Apply decision-making skills in collaborative planning — agree on options within constraints, justify choices, express preferences; work in teams to solve problems using target language; create promotional materials for events; plan for real audiences.
wider: Design and run a simulated transaction scenario — buying, selling, negotiating and justifying decisions with a real partner
Create a complete plan specifying who, what, when, where and how — with a justification for each decision in the target language

response_modes.reason: Decision-making in collaborative contexts integrates preference expression (N1) with constraint management and shared outcome production. Real-stakes tasks make the integration condition authentic.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Using the target language for genuine decision-making — real constraints, real audiences — is where language use becomes genuinely purposeful across curriculum domains.
success_criteria: Participates in a decision-making task expressing at least two justified choices in the target language
Contributes to a shared outcome that reflects the group's negotiated decisions
